data.eyebrow: ALRUE IMPORT BUILDING · LONG ISLAND CITY, NY
body: The Anton Group at Marcus & Millichap is pleased to present this Broker Opinion of Value for 10–40 45th Avenue — the Alrue Import Building, a 60,000-square-foot light-industrial and office-flex asset on one of Long Island City’s best-connected corners. With over 60 years of experience across Manhattan and the outer boroughs, our team has sold, financed, and structured more than $27 billion in office, industrial, retail, and development real estate.

Built in 1931 and renovated in 2006, the three-story-plus-grade building offers M1-4 zoning, four loading docks, three drive-in bays, and immediate access to the 7 and G trains at Court Square and the LIRR. The property is currently almost fully leased across eight tenants, with the owner-related occupant vacating 20,000 square feet — allowing a buyer to capture 21,300 square feet of near-term lease-up while Northwest Queens industrial vacancy sits at just 8.4%.

Based on our analysis of comparable industrial, flex, and sale-leaseback transactions along the Long Island City corridor, we estimate the property’s current market value between $18,500,000 and $21,100,000 — with guidance of $19,700,000 — assuming Year 1 net operating income of $1,088,433 at a going-in capitalization rate of 7.0% to 8.0%.

Our team will leverage Marcus & Millichap’s unmatched national buyer network alongside our Global Capital Group’s direct relationships with investors across Asia, Europe, and the Middle East who are actively seeking New York industrial and flex income. We will target 1031-exchange buyers, owner-users, last-mile operators, and family offices, and we greatly appreciate the opportunity to advise on this exceptional asset.
